# Stop AI coding agents installing hallucinated packages

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/ai-agent-hallucinated-packages/


**ExactGround is a free, open-source guard for AI coding agents.** It runs as a hook in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor. Before an `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `bun`, `npx`, `pip`, `uv`, `poetry` or `pdm` install command it can parse runs, it checks each package name against the public npm registry and PyPI. Names that do not exist, versions that were never published, and young look-alikes of popular packages are blocked. Source and install: [github.com/alidaram99/exactground](https://github.com/alidaram99/exactground).

## Why agents need this

A USENIX Security 2025 study (Spracklen et al.) had 16 models write **576,000 code samples**. Of the **2.23 million package recommendations** in them, **440,445 (19.7%) named packages that do not exist**, 205,474 unique names. In a separate test, the authors re-ran 500 prompts that had produced a hallucination 10 times each, and 43% of those hallucinated names came back in all 10 runs ([paper](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity25/presentation/spracklen)). Because the names are predictable, attackers can register them with malware. This is called *slopsquatting*.

A rule in `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` saying "never invent packages" is text the model may ignore. A hook is code that runs on every install.

## Try it in one line

```console
$ npx -y github:alidaram99/exactground#v0.1.3 check pypi:requests pypi:reqeusts react@99.0.0
OK      pypi:requests
BLOCK   pypi:reqeusts — "reqeusts" does not exist on PyPI; did you mean "requests"? (it is 1 edit away)
BLOCK   react@99.0.0 — version 99.0.0 of "react" was never published (latest is 19.3.0)
```

## Install it in your agent

- **Claude Code:** `claude plugin marketplace add alidaram99/exactground`, then `claude plugin install exactground@exactground-marketplace`.
- **Codex:** `codex plugin marketplace add alidaram99/exactground --ref v0.1.3`, then trust the hook in `/hooks`.
- **Gemini CLI and Cursor:** `exactground init gemini --write` or `exactground init cursor --write` in your project.

Installs hidden inside `node -e`, `python -c`, `$(...)` or `eval` cannot be checked, so the hook denies them. If the registry or the checker fails, it denies too.

**Threat model, plainly:** ExactGround stops an agent that hallucinates or mistypes a package name in a normal install command. It is a cooperative guardrail, not a sandbox: an agent that deliberately tries to evade it (by writing its own scripts, editing files the hooks do not see, or running code another way) can get around it. To contain an agent you do not trust, use OS or container sandboxing.

Bare installs such as `npm install`, `uv sync` and `poetry install` are checked against the lockfile, so a dependency the agent wrote into `package.json` or `pyproject.toml` is caught too.

## Check that an API exists in your exact version

Many hallucinations are real packages used wrongly. `useActionState` does not exist in React 18, and `numpy.asfarray` was removed in NumPy 2.0. The hosted ExactGround API answers these questions from the published package itself:
- npm: `.d.ts` declarations, read with the TypeScript compiler.
- Python: wheels, parsed statically and never executed.

Status: live on the Apify Store since October 3, 2026. Calls need your Apify API token.

It is an MCP server billed per check:
- `check_symbols`: $0.002 per symbol.
- `check_packages`: $0.0005 per package.
- `check_diff`: $0.01 per diff.

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http exactground https://dropin-apis--exactground-api.apify.actor/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $APIFY_TOKEN"
```

**[Open ExactGround on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/exactground-api)** · [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/alidaram99/exactground)

# App Store Reviews Scraper: any app, no Connect key

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/app-store-reviews-scraper/


The **App Store Connect API** only gives you reviews for apps your team owns, and it needs a private key. To read what users say about **any** app, including competitors, in any storefront, this Actor collects reviews from Apple's public customer-review feed and adds the app's public metadata. It needs no login and no Connect key.

## What you get

**One row per review:**

| Field | Example |
|---|---|
| `appId`, `appName`, `country` | `570060128`, `Duolingo: Language Lessons`, `us` |
| `reviewId`, `title`, `text`, `rating` (1–5) | `14612250135`, `Fun`, `Very fun and…`, `5` |
| `version`, `date`, `userName` | `7.142.0`, `2026-09-30T13:01:34-07:00`, `…` |
| `voteCount`, `voteSum` | helpfulness votes |

**Optionally, one app-details row per app × country:** name, developer, price and currency, average rating, rating count, version, release dates, genres, content rating, size, minimum OS and description.

App-details row from a real run:

```json
{
  "type": "app",
  "appId": "570060128",
  "country": "us",
  "name": "Duolingo: Language Lessons",
  "developer": "Duolingo, Inc",
  "price": 0,
  "currency": "USD",
  "averageRating": 4.72302,
  "ratingCount": 5481026,
  "version": "7.142.0",
  "currentVersionReleaseDate": "2026-09-28T17:42:01Z",
  "genres": ["Education", "Social Networking"],
  "contentRating": "4+",
  "url": "https://apps.apple.com/us/app/duolingo-language-lessons/id570060128?uo=4"
}
```

## Use cases

- **ASO and product feedback:** pull every recent review of your app into a spreadsheet or database and track ratings by version.
- **Competitor monitoring:** watch a competitor's rating, review volume and release cadence across countries.
- **Market research:** compare what users complain about across the top apps in a category and storefront.

## Run it in the Apify Console (no code)

1. Open the **[App Store Reviews Scraper](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/app-store-reviews)** and click **Try for free**.
2. Paste App Store URLs or numeric app ids, for example `https://apps.apple.com/us/app/duolingo-language-lessons/id570060128` or `570060128`.
3. Choose countries (`us`, `gb`, `de`…), the maximum number of reviews per app, and optionally a `sinceDate`.
4. Click **Start**, then export the dataset as CSV, Excel or JSON.

## Run it from code

Replace `<owner>/app-store-reviews` with the Actor id shown on its Store page.

### Node.js (`apify-client`)

```js
import { ApifyClient } from 'apify-client';

const client = new ApifyClient({ token: process.env.APIFY_TOKEN });

const run = await client.actor('<owner>/app-store-reviews').call({
  apps: ['570060128'], countries: ['us'], maxReviewsPerApp: 50, includeAppDetails: true,
});
const { items } = await client.dataset(run.defaultDatasetId).listItems();
for (const row of items) console.log(row.type, row.type === 'app' ? `${row.name} ★${row.averageRating}` : `${row.rating}★ ${row.title}`);
```

### Python (`apify-client` ≥ 3)

```python
import os
from apify_client import ApifyClient

client = ApifyClient(os.environ["APIFY_TOKEN"])
run = client.actor("<owner>/app-store-reviews").call(
    run_input={"apps": ["570060128"], "countries": ["us", "gb"], "maxReviewsPerApp": 200},
)
for item in client.dataset(run.default_dataset_id).list_items().items:
    print(item["type"], item.get("rating"), item.get("title"))
```

### curl (one call, results in the response)

```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/<owner>~app-store-reviews/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"apps":["570060128"],"countries":["us"],"maxReviewsPerApp":50}'
```

## Limits

- **Up to 500 reviews per app per country.** Apple's public feed stops there (10 pages × 50). To get more coverage, add more `countries`, since reviews differ by storefront.
- Developer replies are not part of Apple's public feed, so `developerResponse` is always `null`.
- Reviews come newest first. `sinceDate` stops paging once older reviews are reached.

## Pricing

**$0.20 per 1,000 rows** ($0.0002 per review or app-details row), pay per event. You pay only for rows delivered, with no subscription.

**[Open the App Store Reviews Scraper on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/app-store-reviews)**

# Azure Content Moderator retirement (Mar 15, 2027): drop-in API

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/azure-content-moderator-alternative/


**Yes: Microsoft deprecated Azure Content Moderator in February 2024 and retires it on March 15, 2027; its successor, Azure AI Content Safety, is a different API with different requests and results** ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-moderator/overview)). To keep code that reads `Terms`, `PII` and `Classification`, point your `ProcessText/Screen` calls at a wire-compatible endpoint such as our [Content Moderator drop-in on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/content-moderator-compat): same request, same JSON, $1 per 1,000 texts.

Microsoft's [lifecycle page](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/lifecycle/products/azure-ai-content-moderator) lists the retirement as April 1, 2027 (06:59 PT). The product notice says March 15, 2027, so plan for **March 15**. If you prefer to move to Content Safety, see [Content Moderator vs Content Safety: what changes](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/azure-content-moderator-to-content-safety/).

## What changes on March 15, 2027

- Existing Content Moderator resources stop being supported. No new Content Moderator projects could be created after March 15, 2024.
- `POST https://<region>.api.cognitive.microsoft.com/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen` and the SDKs built on it (`Microsoft.Azure.CognitiveServices.ContentModerator`, `azure-cognitiveservices-vision-contentmoderator`) lose their service.
- Code, stored results and dashboards that depend on `Terms`, `PII`, `Classification.Category1/2/3`, `ReviewRecommended` or `Status.Code 3000` have no equivalent in Content Safety. It returns severity levels for Hate, Sexual, Violence and SelfHarm instead.

## The minimal migration: host and key only

The new endpoint is the Actor's Standby URL, `https://dropin-apis--content-moderator-compat.apify.actor`. Authenticate with your [Apify API token](https://console.apify.com/settings/integrations) as `Authorization: Bearer …` (or `?token=…`). An `Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key` header is accepted and ignored. Path, query string, raw-text body and response are unchanged.

### curl

```diff
- curl -s -X POST "https://westus.api.cognitive.microsoft.com/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen?language=eng&classify=True&PII=True" \
-   -H "Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key: $AZURE_KEY" \
+ curl -s -X POST "https://dropin-apis--content-moderator-compat.apify.actor/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen?language=eng&classify=True&PII=True" \
+   -H "Authorization: Bearer $APIFY_TOKEN" \
    -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' --data-binary 'Is this a crap email abcdef@abcd.com?'
```

### Python (`requests`)

```diff
- BASE = "https://westus.api.cognitive.microsoft.com"
- AUTH = {"Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key": os.environ["AZURE_KEY"]}
+ BASE = "https://dropin-apis--content-moderator-compat.apify.actor"
+ AUTH = {"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["APIFY_TOKEN"]}
  r = requests.post(f"{BASE}/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen",
                    params={"language": "eng", "classify": "True", "PII": "True"},
                    headers={"Content-Type": "text/plain", **AUTH}, data=text.encode("utf-8"))
```

### Node.js (`fetch`)

```diff
- const BASE = 'https://westus.api.cognitive.microsoft.com';
- const AUTH = { 'Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key': process.env.AZURE_KEY };
+ const BASE = 'https://dropin-apis--content-moderator-compat.apify.actor';
+ const AUTH = { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.APIFY_TOKEN}` };
  const res = await fetch(`${BASE}/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen?language=eng&classify=True`, {
    method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/plain', ...AUTH }, body: text,
  });
```

## Real output on Microsoft's own example

```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://dropin-apis--content-moderator-compat.apify.actor/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen?language=eng&classify=True&PII=True" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APIFY_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' \
  --data-binary 'Is this a crap email abcdef@abcd.com, phone: 6657789887, IP: 255.255.255.255, 1 Microsoft Way, Redmond, WA 98052'
```

Our response matches Microsoft's published `NormalizedText`, the `Terms` entry (`crap` at Index 10) and every PII index:

```json
{
  "OriginalText": "Is this a crap email abcdef@abcd.com, phone: 6657789887, IP: 255.255.255.255, 1 Microsoft Way, Redmond, WA 98052",
  "NormalizedText": "Is this a crap email abcdef@ abcd. com, phone: 6657789887, IP: 255. 255. 255. 255, 1 Microsoft Way, Redmond, WA 98052",
  "Misrepresentation": null,
  "PII": {
    "Email": [{ "Detected": "abcdef@abcd.com", "SubType": "Regular", "Text": "abcdef@abcd.com", "Index": 21 }],
    "SSN": [],
    "IPA": [{ "SubType": "IPV4", "Text": "255.255.255.255", "Index": 61 }],
    "Phone": [{ "CountryCode": "US", "Text": "6657789887", "Index": 45 }],
    "Address": [{ "Text": "1 Microsoft Way, Redmond, WA 98052", "Index": 78 }]
  },
  "Classification": {
    "ReviewRecommended": true,
    "Category1": { "Score": 0.0023 },
    "Category2": { "Score": 0.2708 },
    "Category3": { "Score": 0.9562 }
  },
  "Language": "eng",
  "Terms": [{ "Index": 10, "OriginalIndex": 10, "ListId": 0, "Term": "crap" }],
  "Status": { "Code": 3000, "Description": "OK", "Exception": null },
  "TrackingId": "…"
}
```

### C# (`HttpClient`, .NET 6+)

```csharp
using System.Net.Http.Headers;
using System.Text;
using System.Text.Json;

var baseUrl = "https://dropin-apis--content-moderator-compat.apify.actor";
var token = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("APIFY_TOKEN")!;

using var http = new HttpClient();
http.DefaultRequestHeaders.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", token);

var content = new StringContent("Is this a crap email abcdef@abcd.com?", Encoding.UTF8, "text/plain");
var response = await http.PostAsync(
    $"{baseUrl}/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen?language=eng&classify=True&PII=True", content);
response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();

using var json = JsonDocument.Parse(await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync());
var root = json.RootElement;
Console.WriteLine($"Status {root.GetProperty("Status").GetProperty("Code").GetInt32()}, " +
                  $"Category3 {root.GetProperty("Classification").GetProperty("Category3").GetProperty("Score").GetDouble():F3}, " +
                  $"first term '{root.GetProperty("Terms")[0].GetProperty("Term").GetString()}'");
// Status 3000, Category3 0.971, first term 'crap'
```

If you use the old `Microsoft.Azure.CognitiveServices.ContentModerator` SDK, set `client.Endpoint` to the Standby URL and pass `ServiceClientCredentials` that add the `Authorization: Bearer` header. *We tested the REST path above, not that SDK.*

## Your options compared

| Option | Same ProcessText/Screen request and JSON? | Price | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Content Moderator drop-in on Apify (this page)** | **Yes**: change host and key | **$1 per 1,000 texts** | Terms (24-language open list), PII, Classification. Category scores approximate. No custom term lists, image or video |
| [Azure AI Content Safety](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-safety/overview) | No: `text:analyze` returns severity levels | Free tier 5,000 text records/month (1 record = up to 1,000 characters); paid per Azure pricing | Microsoft's successor. Custom blocklists, 100+ languages. Needs a rewrite and re-tuned thresholds |
| [OpenAI moderation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/moderation) (`omni-moderation-latest`) | No | Free with an OpenAI account | Policy categories; no term offsets or PII |
| Self-host: [Detoxify](https://github.com/unitaryai/detoxify) + [Microsoft Presidio](https://github.com/microsoft/presidio) for PII | No: you build the API | Free (Apache-2.0 / MIT) + your servers | Most control, most work |

If you can rewrite the integration and re-tune thresholds, Content Safety is the supported path. The drop-in is for code, stored results and dashboards that depend on the old response format.

## What is identical, approximate, or unsupported

| Feature | Status |
|---|---|
| Route, method, query parameters (case-insensitive), `text/plain`/`html`/`xml`/`markdown` bodies, 1,024-character limit | **Identical** |
| Field names, casing and order; `Status` 3000; `Terms: null` when clean; `Misrepresentation: null`; `TrackingId` | **Identical** |
| `NormalizedText`; `Terms` `Index` and `OriginalIndex` offsets | Identical on Microsoft's documented examples. Unusual inputs may normalize differently |
| `PII` (Email, IPA, Phone, Address, SSN) | Same shape. Patterns are deliberately strict: US/UK phones, US addresses with state and ZIP |
| Built-in profanity list (`ListId 0`) | Same format. The word list is open (LDNOOBW, CC-BY-4.0, 24 languages), so matches can differ from Azure's private list |
| `Classification` Category1 (explicit), Category3 (offensive) | **Approximate.** Open Detoxify model; scores differ from Azure's |
| `Classification` Category2 (suggestive) | **Approximate proxy:** `max(Category1, 0.3 × obscene)`. Flirty but clean text is not detected |
| `ReviewRecommended` | True when any category is ≥ 0.5. Azure's own thresholds were never published |
| Classification for non-English text | Omitted, as in Azure |
| `autocorrect=true` | Accepted. The field is returned, but no spelling correction is applied |
| Custom term lists (`listId`), image/video moderation, list management, review tool | **Not supported** |

## Pricing

**$1 per 1,000 screened texts**, pay per event.
- Requests that fail validation are not charged.
- There is no subscription.
- You can cap spending per run on Apify (`429 TooManyRequests` at the cap).

## FAQ

### Is Azure Content Moderator being retired?

Yes. Microsoft deprecated it in February 2024 and retires it on March 15, 2027. Microsoft's lifecycle table lists April 1, 2027, but the product notice says March 15, 2027, so plan for March 15.

### What replaces Azure Content Moderator?

Microsoft's replacement is Azure AI Content Safety, which uses a different API: `text:analyze` with severity levels for Hate, Sexual, Violence and SelfHarm. To keep the old `ProcessText/Screen` request and JSON, use a wire-compatible endpoint such as this page's drop-in.

### How do I migrate from Azure Content Moderator without rewriting code?

Change the host from `<region>.api.cognitive.microsoft.com` to the drop-in's Standby URL and send your Apify token as `Authorization: Bearer …` instead of `Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key`. The path, query parameters, body and response JSON stay the same.

### Should I just move to Content Safety?

If you can rewrite the integration and re-tune thresholds, yes, that is Microsoft's supported path. This replacement is for teams whose code, stored results and dashboards depend on the old response format.

### Are custom term lists supported?

No. The drop-in supports the built-in profanity list (`ListId 0`), PII and classification. Custom term lists, image and video moderation are not supported.

### Do you store text?

No. Nothing is written to disk or logged.

### How are short non-English texts handled?

Latin-script text under 40 characters is treated as English. Pass `language=spa`, `language=deu` and so on to use the right profanity list.

## Get started

**[Azure Content Moderator drop-in on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/content-moderator-compat)**: copy its Standby URL and your token, then change the endpoint in your code.

# Azure Content Moderator vs Content Safety: what changes (2027)

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/azure-content-moderator-to-content-safety/


**Azure AI Content Safety is not a new version of Content Moderator's API: it has a different endpoint (`text:analyze`), JSON body and result (severity levels for Hate, Sexual, Violence and SelfHarm), so migrating means rewriting the call and re-mapping your thresholds** ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-moderator/overview)). Content Moderator retires on March 15, 2027. If you would rather not rewrite before then, a [wire-compatible Content Moderator replacement](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/azure-content-moderator-alternative/) keeps `ProcessText/Screen` working with only a host and key change.

## The two requests side by side

**Content Moderator (retiring):**

```bash
curl -X POST "https://<region>.api.cognitive.microsoft.com/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen?language=eng&classify=True&PII=True" \
  -H "Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: text/plain" \
  --data-binary 'Is this a crap email abcdef@abcd.com?'
```

**Content Safety (Microsoft's replacement),** per Microsoft's [text quickstart](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-safety/quickstart-text):

```bash
curl -X POST "<endpoint>/contentsafety/text:analyze?api-version=2024-09-01" \
  -H "Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text": "Is this a crap email abcdef@abcd.com?", "categories": ["Hate", "Sexual", "SelfHarm", "Violence"], "outputType": "FourSeverityLevels"}'
```

Content Safety returns `categoriesAnalysis` (for example `{"category": "Hate", "severity": 2}`) and `blocklistsMatch`. Severities are `0, 2, 4, 6` (four levels) or `0–7` (eight levels).

## Field-by-field mapping

| Content Moderator `ProcessText/Screen` | Content Safety `text:analyze` | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Raw text body (`text/plain`, `html`, `xml`, `markdown`) | JSON `{"text": "..."}` | Body format changes |
| Query `language`, `classify`, `PII`, `autocorrect`, `listId` | JSON `categories`, `blocklistNames`, `haltOnBlocklistHit`, `outputType` | Different parameters |
| `Terms[]` (built-in profanity list, `ListId 0`, with `Index`/`OriginalIndex`) | `blocklistsMatch[]` from **your own** blocklists | No built-in profanity list with offsets |
| `PII` (Email, IPA, Phone, Address, SSN with indexes) | None | Use a separate PII service, such as Azure AI Language PII detection |
| `Classification.Category1` (explicit), `Category2` (suggestive), `Category3` (offensive), each 0–1 | `Sexual`, `Hate`, `Violence`, `SelfHarm` severity levels | No 1:1 mapping; re-tune thresholds |
| `Classification.ReviewRecommended` | None | Derive from your own severity thresholds |
| `NormalizedText`, `AutoCorrectedText`, `Misrepresentation` | None | |
| `Status.Code 3000`, `TrackingId` | HTTP status and error body | Error handling changes |
| Image, video moderation | Image analysis (separate endpoint) | |

## Which way to go

| Situation | Path |
|---|---|
| You can rewrite the call and re-tune thresholds before March 2027 | Move to Content Safety (Microsoft's supported path; free tier of 5,000 text records a month) |
| Your code, stored results or dashboards depend on `Terms`, `PII` or `Category1/2/3` | Keep the format with a [wire-compatible replacement](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/azure-content-moderator-alternative/) ($1 per 1,000 texts) and migrate later on your own schedule |
| You only need a free generic moderation signal | OpenAI's `omni-moderation-latest` (free), also with a different API |

The minimal change with the wire-compatible replacement:

```diff
- POST https://<region>.api.cognitive.microsoft.com/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen?language=eng&classify=True
- Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key: $AZURE_KEY
+ POST https://dropin-apis--content-moderator-compat.apify.actor/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen?language=eng&classify=True
+ Authorization: Bearer $APIFY_TOKEN
```

## FAQ

### Is Azure Content Safety the same API as Content Moderator?

No. Content Safety uses `POST /contentsafety/text:analyze` with a JSON body and returns severity levels for Hate, Sexual, Violence and SelfHarm. Content Moderator's `ProcessText/Screen` took a raw text body and returned `Terms`, `PII` and `Classification` scores.

### Does Content Safety detect PII like Content Moderator did?

Not in `text:analyze`. Content Moderator's `PII` output (email, phone, IP, address, SSN) has no equivalent there, so you need a separate PII detection service or a wire-compatible replacement.

### How do Content Moderator categories map to Content Safety?

Roughly: Category1 (sexually explicit) and Category2 (suggestive) relate to Sexual, and Category3 (offensive) overlaps with Hate and Violence. The scales differ (0–1 scores versus severity levels), so thresholds must be re-tuned on your own data.

### When does Azure Content Moderator stop working?

Microsoft says it retires on March 15, 2027. Microsoft's lifecycle table lists April 1, 2027; plan for March 15.

### Can I keep using ProcessText/Screen after the retirement?

Not on Azure. A wire-compatible replacement accepts the same `ProcessText/Screen` request and returns the same JSON from a new host.

# Check if an npm or PyPI Package Exists — API & MCP

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/check-npm-package-exists-api/


**This API answers one question an AI coding agent can't answer on its own: does this npm or PyPI package exist, and does the function or method it's about to call actually exist in the exact version pinned in your lockfile?** It reads the published package itself — TypeScript `.d.ts` declarations, DefinitelyTyped, Python wheel source and `.pyi` stubs — without running any of its code, and answers over MCP or REST.

## Why this exists

A USENIX Security 2025 study (Spracklen et al.) had 16 models write **576,000 code samples**. Of the **2.23 million package recommendations** in them, **440,445 (19.7%) named packages that do not exist**, 205,474 unique names. In a separate test, the authors re-ran 500 prompts that had produced a hallucination 10 times each, and 43% of those hallucinated names came back in all 10 runs ([paper](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity25/presentation/spracklen)). Predictable names are what make "slopsquatting" (registering the invented name with malware) practical.

The quieter failure is calling a real API that isn't in *your* version — `useActionState` exists in React 19 but not React 18; `numpy.asfarray` was removed in NumPy 2.0. The code looks right, passes review, and breaks at runtime.

## What it checks

| Endpoint | Question it answers | Price |
|---|---|---|
| `check_symbols` / `POST /v1/symbols` | Does `symbol` exist in `package@version`? Returns `exists`, kind, signature, deprecation notes and did-you-mean suggestions | $0.002 per symbol |
| `check_packages` / `POST /v1/packages` | Does the package exist? Was the pinned version published? Is it a look-alike of a popular package, brand new, or an npm security placeholder? | $0.0005 per package |
| `check_diff` / `POST /v1/diff` | For a diff: every added import, and whether each imported name exists in the pinned version | $0.01 per diff |

`exists: null` means "cannot be known statically" (a dynamic Python `__getattr__`, a compiled extension, or an untyped npm package) — it is never reported as a guess.

## Example (real output)

```bash
curl -s https://dropin-apis--exactground-api.apify.actor/v1/symbols \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APIFY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"ecosystem":"pypi","package":"numpy","version":"2.1.0","symbols":["numpy.linalg.norm","numpy.asfarray"]}'
```

```json
{
  "ecosystem": "pypi", "package": "numpy", "version": "2.1.0", "packageExists": true,
  "results": [
    { "symbol": "numpy.linalg.norm", "exists": true, "kind": "function" },
    { "symbol": "numpy.asfarray", "exists": false, "missingAt": "numpy.asfarray",
      "suggestions": ["array", "asarray", "NDArray", "ndarray", "recarray"] }
  ]
}
```

A package check on a typo'd name:

```json
{ "ecosystem": "pypi", "name": "reqeusts", "verdict": "block", "registry": "missing",
  "reasons": ["\"reqeusts\" does not exist on PyPI", "did you mean \"requests\"? (it is 1 edit away)"] }
```

## How it compares

| Tool | Answers | What it's for |
|---|---|---|
| **This Actor** | Yes/no, from the published artifact itself | Does this exact name/version/symbol exist |
| Context7 | Documentation text for a prompt | What does this library's docs say |
| Socket | Security score for packages that exist | Is this existing package malicious or risky |

Context7 and Socket solve different, adjacent problems — this tool is the one that catches a name or API that was never real in the first place.

## Connect an agent (MCP)

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http exactground https://dropin-apis--exactground-api.apify.actor/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $APIFY_TOKEN"
```

Also works with Cursor, VS Code, Codex and any MCP-compatible client (`mcp.json` or `~/.codex/config.toml`), and can be found by agents on the [Apify MCP server](https://mcp.apify.com) via `search-actors`.

## Pricing

Pay per event, no subscription. A typical agent session (5 package checks, 20 symbol checks, 2 diffs) costs about **$0.06**. Requests that fail (invalid input, registry unreachable) are not charged; setting a maximum total charge stops the API with HTTP 402 once reached.

**[Open ExactGround on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/exactground-api)** · [Free local install guard](https://github.com/alidaram99/exactground)

## FAQ

### How do I stop Claude Code or Cursor from installing hallucinated packages?

Install the free [ExactGround hook](https://github.com/alidaram99/exactground) — it blocks `npm`/`pnpm`/`yarn`/`bun`/`npx` and `pip`/`uv`/`poetry`/`pdm`/`pipx` installs of names that don't exist, before they run. This API adds version-exact function/method checks on top.

### What is slopsquatting?

Attackers publish malware under package names AI models tend to invent. When an agent runs an install command on the invented name, it installs the attacker's code instead.

### How is this different from Context7?

Context7 puts documentation text into the prompt. This API answers a yes/no question from the published artifact itself — does a given symbol exist in a given version — and returns a verdict (`ok`, `warn` or `block`). It does not intercept installs itself; the free local ExactGround hook is what refuses an install in your agent.

### Which languages are supported?

npm (JavaScript and TypeScript) and PyPI (Python).

### Is my code sent anywhere?

Only what you send in a request — package names and symbol paths, or a diff for `check_diff`. Nothing is stored after the response.

### Is this affiliated with npm, PyPI, Anthropic, OpenAI or Cursor?

No. It is an independent tool.

# Extract All URLs From a Sitemap — indexes, gzip, robots.txt

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/extract-urls-from-sitemap/


**Give this Actor a domain or sitemap URL, and it returns one row per page URL from the site's public sitemap** — it does not open or crawl those pages, only the sitemap files themselves. It follows sitemap indexes, unpacks `.xml.gz`, and checks `robots.txt` for `Sitemap:` lines.

## What it looks up

Given a domain, it checks (in order): `robots.txt` (every `Sitemap:` line), then `/sitemap.xml` and `/sitemap_index.xml` if not already listed. A start URL that already ends in `.xml` or `.xml.gz` is fetched directly. An index is followed one child file at a time until `maxUrls` is reached; a file starting with the gzip magic bytes is unpacked automatically.

## Example input

```json
{
  "startUrls": [{ "url": "https://www.sitemaps.org" }],
  "maxUrls": 10
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `startUrls` | required | A domain or a sitemap URL (`.xml` or `.xml.gz`) |
| `includeRegex` / `excludeRegex` | optional | Case-insensitive regex to keep or drop matching URLs |
| `lastmodSince` | optional | ISO date — URLs with an older `lastmod` are dropped; URLs with no `lastmod` are kept |
| `maxUrls` | integer, default 1000 | Stop after this many unique URLs |

## Example output

```json
{
  "url": "https://www.sitemaps.org/",
  "lastmod": "2016-11-21",
  "changefreq": null,
  "priority": null,
  "sourceSitemap": "https://www.sitemaps.org/sitemap.xml",
  "domain": "www.sitemaps.org"
}
```

Both a real sitemap index (`https://apify.com`) and a gzip child sitemap (`https://www.gnu.org`'s `sitemap0.xml.gz`) were checked against live sites during development.

## Use cases

- **A URL list for another Actor or crawler** that only needs the links, not a fresh crawl of the whole site.
- **Change detection** — keep rows whose `lastmod` is after a date you pass in.
- **A scoped export** — keep or drop URLs with a regular expression (`/blog/`, a locale, a file type).

## Limits

Public `http`/`https` sitemaps only, no login; private hosts are refused. At most 50 sitemap files per run and 20 MB per file after unpacking. At most 5 fetches in flight, with retries on HTTP 429/5xx, and `Crawl-delay` in robots.txt honored up to 5 seconds. A path disallowed for `User-agent: *` is not fetched. The run **fails** if every input produces zero URLs, so an empty success is never silently reported as a finished dataset.

## Run it from code

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/dropin-apis~sitemap-url-extractor/run-sync-get-dataset-items" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"startUrls":[{"url":"https://www.sitemaps.org"}],"maxUrls":10}'
```

## Pricing

Pay per event — the primary event is `apify-default-dataset-item` at **$0.0004 per URL ($0.40 per 1,000)**, charged when a row is saved. No monthly fee.

**[Open Sitemap URL Extractor & Scraper on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/sitemap-url-extractor)**

## FAQ

### Does this crawl the pages listed in the sitemap?

No. It only downloads sitemap files and returns the URLs listed inside them — it never fetches the pages those URLs point to.

### What if the site publishes a sitemap index or a `.gz` file?

A sitemap index is followed one child file at a time until `maxUrls` is reached. A file that starts with the gzip magic bytes is unpacked automatically — both paths were checked against real live sites, not only synthetic fixtures.

### What does a plain domain input actually fetch?

`/robots.txt` first (reading every `Sitemap:` line), then `/sitemap.xml` and `/sitemap_index.xml` if those weren't already listed there. A start URL ending in `.xml` or `.xml.gz` is fetched directly, skipping the robots.txt step.

### Why did the run fail with "0 URL(s)"?

None of the inputs had a readable public sitemap. A missing `/sitemap_index.xml` on its own is normal and not a failure — the failure only triggers when every candidate sitemap was missing or wasn't valid sitemap XML.

### What does it cost?

$0.0004 per extracted URL ($0.40 per 1,000 rows), pay per event, with no subscription.

# Drop-in replacements for retiring APIs, plus data tools

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/


Three widely used APIs are being switched off between December 2026 and March 2027. Their official successors use **different requests and responses**, so every integration has to be rewritten. The tools below accept **the same request and return the same response shape** as the API you already call. You change the host, add an Apify token, and keep your code.

They run on [Apify](https://apify.com) and are billed per use, with no subscription. Each one says clearly what is identical, what is approximate and what is not supported.

## Drop-in replacements

### Google Perspective API (ends after 31 Dec 2026)
`POST /v1alpha1/comments:analyze`, with TOXICITY, INSULT, THREAT, PROFANITY, IDENTITY_ATTACK, SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT and SEVERE_TOXICITY, in 7 languages. Google's own Python client works with only the discovery URL changed. Scores come from open models: close to Perspective's, not identical.
**$1 per 1,000 comments** · [Migration guide](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/perspective-api-alternative/) · [Apify Store](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/perspective-compat) · [Shutdown checklist](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/perspective-api-shutdown-checklist/)

### Azure Content Moderator, text screen (retires 15 Mar 2027)
`POST /contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen`, with the same `Terms`, `PII`, `Classification` and `Status` JSON. It matches Microsoft's own documented example field for field. Category scores are approximate, and custom term lists are not supported.
**$1 per 1,000 texts** · [Migration guide](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/azure-content-moderator-alternative/) · [Apify Store](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/content-moderator-compat) · [Content Moderator vs Content Safety](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/azure-content-moderator-to-content-safety/)

### OpenAI whisper-1 (removed 26 Feb 2027)
`/v1/audio/transcriptions` and `/translations`, with SRT, VTT, and word and segment timestamps. It works with the official OpenAI Python and Node SDKs by changing `base_url` and `api_key`. It uses the smaller open Whisper model (about 4% word error on clear English), with up to 10 minutes per file.
**$0.006 per minute** · [Migration guide](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/whisper-1-alternative/) · [Apify Store](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/whisper-compat) · [All OpenAI transcription models removed Feb 26, 2027](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/openai-transcription-models-deprecation-2027/)

## Data tools

### App Store reviews
Reviews and app details for any app in any country, from Apple's public feed, with no App Store Connect key. Up to 500 reviews per app per country.
**$0.20 per 1,000 rows** · [Guide](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/app-store-reviews-scraper/) · [Apify Store](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/app-store-reviews)

### Woolworths Australia prices
Shelf price, specials and unit price per kg or litre, by search term, from public catalog data.
**$1 per 1,000 products** · [Guide](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/woolworths-api/) · [Apify Store](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/woolworths-au-products)

## How it works

1. Create a free Apify account and copy your API token.
2. Open the tool on the Apify Store. For the API replacements, copy its **Standby URL**.
3. Point your existing code at that URL and send the token. Pay only for what you use, and set a spending cap if you like.

Nothing you send is stored: comments, texts and audio are processed in memory and discarded.

# OpenAI removes whisper-1 and gpt-4o-transcribe on Feb 26, 2027

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/openai-transcription-models-deprecation-2027/


**On August 26, 2026, OpenAI told developers that `whisper-1`, `gpt-4o-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe` and `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize` will all be removed from the API on February 26, 2027, and recommended `gpt-transcribe` or `gpt-live-transcribe` instead** ([OpenAI deprecations, "2026-08-26: Transcription models"](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)). Plain transcription can usually move to `gpt-transcribe` by changing the model name. Apps that rely on whisper-1-only features (SRT/VTT subtitles, word timestamps, `/v1/audio/translations`) need either a rewrite or a [whisper-1-compatible endpoint](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/whisper-1-alternative/).

## What is removed on February 26, 2027

| Model | Removed | OpenAI's recommended replacement |
|---|---|---|
| `whisper-1` | February 26, 2027 | `gpt-transcribe` or `gpt-live-transcribe` |
| `gpt-4o-transcribe` | February 26, 2027 | `gpt-transcribe` or `gpt-live-transcribe` |
| `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe` | February 26, 2027 | `gpt-transcribe` or `gpt-live-transcribe` |
| `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize` | February 26, 2027 | `gpt-transcribe` or `gpt-live-transcribe` |

Related: OpenAI's deprecations page also lists `tts-1` and `tts-1-hd` (text-to-speech) for removal on January 6, 2027, with `gpt-realtime-2.1-mini` recommended.

## Which replacement fits your use

| You use the model for… | Simplest path | What to check |
|---|---|---|
| Plain text transcripts (`json` / `text`) | Change `model` to `gpt-transcribe` | Accuracy and cost on your audio |
| Subtitles (`srt`, `vtt`) or word/segment timestamps | A whisper-1-compatible endpoint, such as the [whisper-1 drop-in on Apify](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/whisper-1-alternative/) | OpenAI's speech-to-text guide documents `timestamp_granularities[]` only for whisper-1 |
| Translation to English (`/v1/audio/translations`) | A whisper-1-compatible endpoint | OpenAI's guide documents `/v1/audio/translations` only with whisper-1 |
| Live captions | `gpt-live-transcribe` | Realtime API usage differs from file upload |
| Speaker labels (`diarized_json`) | Re-test on `gpt-transcribe`, or a separate diarization step | Output shape changes |

## Prices

| Model | Price (OpenAI pricing page, October 2026) | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `whisper-1` (listed as "Whisper") | $0.006 / minute | Removed Feb 26, 2027 |
| `gpt-4o-transcribe` | token-based, estimated $0.006 / minute | Removed Feb 26, 2027 |
| `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe` | token-based, estimated $0.003 / minute | Removed Feb 26, 2027 |
| `gpt-transcribe` | $0.0045 / minute | Recommended |
| `gpt-live-transcribe` | $0.017 / minute | Recommended (realtime) |
| whisper-1 drop-in on Apify | $0.006 / minute, billed per started 15 s | Independent; Whisper *small* model |

Source: [OpenAI pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing).

## Keeping whisper-1's API: the two-line change

If you need whisper-1's exact request and response formats after February 26, 2027, keep `model="whisper-1"` and point the official SDK at a compatible endpoint:

```diff
- client = OpenAI(api_key=os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"])
+ client = OpenAI(base_url="https://dropin-apis--whisper-compat.apify.actor/v1", api_key=os.environ["APIFY_TOKEN"])
```

The full guide, with Node.js and curl examples, real SRT output and limits, is on the [whisper-1 replacement page](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/whisper-1-alternative/).

## FAQ

### Is gpt-4o-transcribe being deprecated?

Yes. OpenAI's August 26, 2026 notice removes `gpt-4o-transcribe`, together with `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize` and `whisper-1`, from the API on February 26, 2027.

### What replaces gpt-4o-transcribe and whisper-1?

OpenAI recommends `gpt-transcribe`, or `gpt-live-transcribe` for realtime audio.

### When exactly are OpenAI's old transcription models removed?

February 26, 2027, for all four models.

### Does gpt-transcribe support SRT, VTT and word timestamps?

OpenAI's speech-to-text guide documents `timestamp_granularities[]` and the translations endpoint only for whisper-1. Test the subtitle formats you need on `gpt-transcribe` before migrating, or use a whisper-1-compatible endpoint.

### Is gpt-transcribe cheaper than whisper-1?

Yes, on OpenAI's October 2026 price list: $0.0045 per minute versus $0.006 per minute for whisper-1.

# PDF to Markdown API for RAG — DOCX & HTML too

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/pdf-to-markdown-api/


**This Actor converts public PDF, DOCX, HTML, TXT and Markdown URLs into Markdown**, with word count, source title and optional overlapping chunks for retrieval-augmented generation. It reads each document's text layer; it does not perform OCR on scanned pages.

## What it converts

| Format | How | Limits |
|---|---|---|
| PDF | PDF.js text layer; inferred headings, lists and simple aligned tables | First 20 pages by default, maximum 200. Complex multi-column layouts are best effort. |
| DOCX | Mammoth: headings, paragraphs, lists and tables | Public Word files only, no external files or image downloads. |
| HTML | Mozilla Readability article extraction, then Turndown Markdown | Static HTML only — no browser rendering, login or CAPTCHA bypass. |
| TXT / MD | UTF-8 text | TXT is escaped as plain text; Markdown is kept as-is. |

## Example input

```json
{
  "urls": [
    "https://www.w3.org/WAI/ER/tests/xhtml/testfiles/resources/pdf/dummy.pdf",
    "https://example.com/"
  ],
  "maxPages": 2,
  "includeImagesAlt": true,
  "chunkSize": 1200,
  "chunkOverlap": 100
}
```

`urls` accepts 1–20 public HTTP(S) URLs, processed sequentially. `chunkSize: 0` disables chunking; otherwise 200–20,000 Unicode code points, with overlap at most half the chunk size.

## Example output

```json
{
  "url": "https://www.w3.org/WAI/ER/tests/xhtml/testfiles/resources/pdf/dummy.pdf",
  "contentType": "application/pdf",
  "title": "dummy.pdf",
  "markdown": "<!-- Page 1 -->\n\nDummy PDF file",
  "pages": 1,
  "wordCount": 3,
  "chunks": [],
  "warnings": ["PDF headings, reading order and tables are inferred from the text layer; complex layouts may need review."]
}
```

Each chunk, when `chunkSize` is set, carries `index`, `start`, `end`, `text`, with offsets counted in Unicode code points of the returned Markdown.

## How it compares

| Option | OCR | Arabic text | RAG chunking | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **This Actor** | No (text layer only) | Yes — logical Unicode order, not reversed | Built in, overlap configurable | $0.0045 per converted page (PDF), or per 2,000-word block (HTML/DOCX/TXT/MD) |
| A full OCR pipeline | Yes | Varies | Usually a separate step | Typically higher per-page cost |
| Copy-pasting manually | N/A | Manual | Manual | Your time |

This Actor does not do OCR — a scanned or image-only PDF page returns an explicit warning and no text, with no hidden OCR surcharge. Use a dedicated OCR product for scans.

## Run it from code

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/dropin-apis~document-to-markdown/run-sync-get-dataset-items" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"urls":["https://example.com/"],"chunkSize":1200}'
```

In [Apify's MCP server](https://mcp.apify.com), search for `document-to-markdown` and call it with `call-actor` using the input above.

## Pricing

**$0.0045 per converted page-equivalent**, plus **$0.0005 per Actor start** at the default 512 MB. A one-page PDF costs $0.005; a two-page text PDF costs $0.0095; ten short HTML documents in one run cost $0.0455. Failed conversions have no page charge.

**[Open Document to Markdown on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/document-to-markdown)**

## FAQ

### Can it read scanned PDFs or images?

No. A scanned or blank PDF page returns an explicit warning and no text — there is no hidden OCR surcharge. Use a dedicated OCR product for scanned documents.

### Does it preserve every PDF table and column?

No. PDF text coordinates infer heading sizes, lists and simple aligned tables; complex multi-column pages, rotated content and inaccurate font maps can need review. DOCX and HTML use their own document structure directly.

### Does it handle Arabic text correctly?

Yes for text-layer content. Arabic DOCX and HTML retain logical Unicode text, including mixed Latin words and numbers. PDF.js extracts Arabic from real text-layer PDFs without reversing characters, though arbitrary PDF glyph-mapping errors in a source file cannot be universally repaired.

### What does one page cost?

$0.0045 per converted page for PDF (only pages with extracted text are charged), or one event per started 2,000-word block for HTML/DOCX/TXT/MD, plus a one-time $0.0005 Actor-start fee per run at default memory.

### Is this a persistent API I can call anytime?

It's a batch Actor: start a run with your URLs, then read the dataset. It needs no subscription, external OCR key, or separately hosted server, and works from the Apify Console, the run API above, or an MCP-connected agent.

# Perspective API shutdown (Dec 31, 2026): drop-in replacement

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/perspective-api-alternative/


**Yes: Google's Perspective API stops serving requests after December 31, 2026, and Google is not offering migration support** ([perspectiveapi.com](https://perspectiveapi.com/)). To keep existing `comments:analyze` code working, point it at a wire-compatible replacement such as our [Perspective drop-in on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/perspective-compat): it takes the same request and returns the same `attributeScores` JSON for $1 per 1,000 comments, and you change only the host and the key.

Google's own words: the API "will no longer be in service after 2026", usage and quota requests were "addressed until February 2026", and "we will not be offering direct migration support". The scores in our replacement come from open models of the same family (Detoxify), so they are **close to Perspective's but not identical**. See [How the scores compare](#how-the-scores-compare). Planning the switch step by step? Use the [Perspective shutdown migration checklist](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/perspective-api-shutdown-checklist/).

## What changes on January 1, 2027

After December 31, 2026 the service is gone, so these stop working:

- Every request to `https://commentanalyzer.googleapis.com/v1alpha1/comments:analyze`. That covers REST, Google's `googleapiclient`, the `perspective-api-client` npm package, R's `peRspective` and similar.
- `comments:suggestscore` and anything else on that host.
- Plugins that hard-code the host, such as the Discourse plugin and many Discord moderation bots.
- Research and benchmark code that uses Perspective's TOXICITY score as a metric.

New keys and quota increases already ended in February 2026, so you cannot get a new Google key to buy time.

## The minimal migration: host and key only

The new endpoint is the Actor's Standby URL, `https://dropin-apis--perspective-compat.apify.actor`. Authenticate with your [Apify API token](https://console.apify.com/settings/integrations), either as `Authorization: Bearer …` or as `?token=…`. A leftover Google `key=` parameter is accepted and ignored. The request body and the response are unchanged.

### curl

```diff
- curl -s -X POST "https://commentanalyzer.googleapis.com/v1alpha1/comments:analyze?key=$GOOGLE_API_KEY" \
+ curl -s -X POST "https://dropin-apis--perspective-compat.apify.actor/v1alpha1/comments:analyze" \
+   -H "Authorization: Bearer $APIFY_TOKEN" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"comment":{"text":"You are an idiot"},"requestedAttributes":{"TOXICITY":{}}}'
```

### Python (`requests`)

```diff
- URL = "https://commentanalyzer.googleapis.com/v1alpha1/comments:analyze?key=" + GOOGLE_API_KEY
- HEADERS = {}
+ URL = "https://dropin-apis--perspective-compat.apify.actor/v1alpha1/comments:analyze"
+ HEADERS = {"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["APIFY_TOKEN"]}
  r = requests.post(URL, headers=HEADERS, json={"comment": {"text": text}, "requestedAttributes": {"TOXICITY": {}}})
  score = r.json()["attributeScores"]["TOXICITY"]["summaryScore"]["value"]
```

### Node.js (`fetch`)

```diff
- const url = `https://commentanalyzer.googleapis.com/v1alpha1/comments:analyze?key=${process.env.GOOGLE_API_KEY}`;
- const headers = { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' };
+ const url = 'https://dropin-apis--perspective-compat.apify.actor/v1alpha1/comments:analyze';
+ const headers = { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.APIFY_TOKEN}` };
  const res = await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers, body: JSON.stringify({ comment: { text }, requestedAttributes: { TOXICITY: {} } }) });
  const score = (await res.json()).attributeScores.TOXICITY.summaryScore.value;
```

Response (real output from our test run):

```json
{
  "attributeScores": {
    "TOXICITY": {
      "spanScores": [{ "begin": 0, "end": 16, "score": { "value": 0.99683121, "type": "PROBABILITY" } }],
      "summaryScore": { "value": 0.99683121, "type": "PROBABILITY" }
    }
  },
  "languages": ["en"],
  "detectedLanguages": ["en"]
}
```

## Library-specific notes

### Python: Google's own `google-api-python-client`

Keep your Perspective quickstart code. Only the `build()` call changes: point `discoveryServiceUrl` at the Actor and pass your Apify token as credentials.

```python
import os
from googleapiclient import discovery
from google.oauth2.credentials import Credentials

BASE = "https://dropin-apis--perspective-compat.apify.actor"
APIFY_TOKEN = os.environ["APIFY_TOKEN"]

client = discovery.build(
    "commentanalyzer", "v1alpha1",
    credentials=Credentials(APIFY_TOKEN),  # was: developerKey=GOOGLE_API_KEY
    discoveryServiceUrl=BASE + "/$discovery/rest?version={apiVersion}&token=" + APIFY_TOKEN,
    static_discovery=False,
)
response = client.comments().analyze(body={
    "comment": {"text": "friendly greetings from python"},
    "requestedAttributes": {"TOXICITY": {}},
}).execute()
print(response["attributeScores"]["TOXICITY"]["summaryScore"]["value"])  # 0.01015937
```

### Node.js: the `perspective-api-client` npm package

The package hard-codes Google's URL and **bundles its own copy of axios**, so an interceptor on your app's `axios` has no effect. Attach the redirect to the axios instance the library actually loads, once at startup:

```js
const libAxios = require(require.resolve('axios', { paths: [require.resolve('perspective-api-client')] }));
const BASE = 'https://dropin-apis--perspective-compat.apify.actor';

libAxios.interceptors.request.use((cfg) => {
  if (cfg.url && cfg.url.startsWith('https://commentanalyzer.googleapis.com')) {
    cfg.url = cfg.url.replace('https://commentanalyzer.googleapis.com', BASE);
    cfg.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${process.env.APIFY_TOKEN}`;
  }
  return cfg;
});

// unchanged application code:
const Perspective = require('perspective-api-client');
const perspective = new Perspective({ apiKey: 'unused-but-required-by-the-library' });
perspective.analyze('You are a complete moron', { attributes: ['toxicity', 'insult'] })
  .then((r) => console.log(r.attributeScores.TOXICITY.summaryScore.value)); // 0.99700852
```

### Discourse (`discourse-perspective-api`)

The plugin keeps the API key as a site setting, but the host is the constant `GOOGLE_API_DOMAIN = "https://commentanalyzer.googleapis.com"` in `lib/discourse_perspective.rb`. In a fork:
- change that constant to your Standby URL;
- append `token=<APIFY_TOKEN>` to the request query.

The plugin's models (`TOXICITY`, `SEVERE_TOXICITY`) and thresholds work as before. *We have not run this inside a live Discourse instance. The request and response format is what we tested.*

## Your options compared

| Option | Same request and JSON as Perspective? | Attributes | Price | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Perspective drop-in on Apify (this page)** | **Yes**: change host and key | TOXICITY, SEVERE_TOXICITY, INSULT, THREAT, IDENTITY_ATTACK, PROFANITY, SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT (en) | **$1 per 1,000 comments** | Open Detoxify models; scores close, not identical. 7 languages. Nothing stored |
| Self-host [Detoxify](https://github.com/unitaryai/detoxify) | No: Python library, your own API wrapper | toxicity, severe_toxicity, obscene, threat, insult, identity_attack, sexual_explicit | Free (Apache-2.0) + your servers | The same model family we run; you operate it |
| [OpenAI moderation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/moderation) (`omni-moderation-latest`) | No: different endpoint, categories and response | harassment, hate, violence, sexual, self-harm and more | Free with an OpenAI account | Policy categories, not Perspective attributes; thresholds must be re-tuned |
| [Azure AI Content Safety](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-safety/overview) | No: different endpoint and severity scale | Hate, Sexual, Violence, SelfHarm (severity levels) | Free tier 5,000 text records/month; paid per Azure pricing | Azure account and resource required |

If you can rewrite the integration and re-tune thresholds, any of the alternatives is reasonable. The drop-in is for code, stored scores and dashboards that depend on Perspective's exact request and response.

## Supported attributes and languages

| Attribute | en | es fr it pt ru tr | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| TOXICITY, SEVERE_TOXICITY, INSULT, THREAT, IDENTITY_ATTACK | ✅ | ✅ | |
| PROFANITY | ✅ | ✅ | Approximated from the model's "obscene" output |
| SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT | ✅ | — | English only, as in Perspective |
| `*_EXPERIMENTAL` aliases | ✅ | ✅ | Served by the matching base attribute and returned under the name you requested |
| FLIRTATION, the NYT models, bridging attributes | ❌ | ❌ | Returns Perspective's own `LANGUAGE_NOT_SUPPORTED_BY_ATTRIBUTE` error |

- The language is detected automatically when you leave out `languages`. Other languages get Perspective's standard "does not support request languages" error, so your existing fallback code keeps working.
- `spanAnnotations`, `scoreThreshold`, `clientToken` and snake_case field names are supported.
- The limit is 20 KB of text per comment.

## How the scores compare

The scores come from [Detoxify](https://github.com/unitaryai/detoxify), open models trained on the same Jigsaw/Civil Comments data family that Perspective came from. They run as quantized ONNX on CPU inside the Actor: `unbiased-toxic-roberta` for English and `multilingual-toxic-xlm-roberta` for the other six languages.

- Clear cases agree. In our tests, abusive text scored 0.99+ and polite text scored under 0.02.
- **Borderline comments can differ** from Perspective by a noticeable margin. We have not run a side-by-side calibration against the live Perspective API.
- If you auto-hide comments at a high threshold (0.85–0.9), you will probably see similar behavior. If you act at low thresholds, run a sample of your own comments through the Actor's batch mode first and re-tune.

## Pricing

**$1 per 1,000 analyzed comments**, pay per event.
- Failed requests (4xx) are not charged.
- There is no subscription.
- You can cap spending per run on Apify. When you reach your limit, the API answers `429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`.

## FAQ

### Is the Perspective API shutting down?

Yes. Google's Perspective API site says the API will no longer be in service after 2026 (after December 31, 2026). Usage and quota requests were only handled until February 2026.

### Does Google offer a migration path for Perspective API?

No. Google says it will not offer direct migration support. It points to other tools inspired by Perspective, but none of them uses the same API.

### What is the best Perspective API replacement?

If you want to keep your code unchanged, use a wire-compatible drop-in that accepts `POST /v1alpha1/comments:analyze` and returns the same `attributeScores` JSON; this page's Actor does that for $1 per 1,000 comments. If you can rewrite your integration, OpenAI's free moderation endpoint, Azure AI Content Safety or a self-hosted Detoxify model also work, with different categories and scores.

### How do I migrate from Perspective API?

Change the host from `commentanalyzer.googleapis.com` to the Actor's Standby URL and replace `?key=GOOGLE_KEY` with your Apify token (`Authorization: Bearer …`). The request body and the response JSON stay the same. Then re-check your thresholds on a sample of real comments.

### Will my toxicity thresholds still work?

For clear-cut text, yes: abusive comments still score above 0.99 and polite ones below 0.02 in our tests. Borderline comments can score differently, so if you act at low thresholds, test a sample first.

### Is this affiliated with Google?

No. It is an independent service that implements the public `commentanalyzer` v1alpha1 interface.

### Do you store comments?

No. Text is scored in memory and discarded.

### How fast is it?

About 10–30 ms per comment on a warm instance. After about 5 minutes without traffic the instance sleeps, and the next request waits a few seconds while it starts.

## Get started

Open the Actor on the Apify Store, then copy its Standby URL and your token: **[Perspective API drop-in on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/perspective-compat)**.

# Perspective API shutdown checklist: migrate before Dec 31, 2026

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/perspective-api-shutdown-checklist/


**Google's Perspective API stops after December 31, 2026, and Google offers no migration support, so every integration has to move before then** ([perspectiveapi.com](https://perspectiveapi.com/)). This checklist takes you from "where do we even call it?" to a tested cutover, whichever replacement you choose.

New Perspective usage and quota requests already ended in February 2026. Treat the quota you have today as the most you will ever get.

## The timeline

| Date | What happens |
|---|---|
| February 2026 | Google stops handling new usage and quota-increase requests |
| Now to mid-December 2026 | Your window to inventory, choose, test and cut over |
| December 31, 2026 | Last day of service ("no longer be in service after 2026") |
| January 1, 2027 | Calls to `commentanalyzer.googleapis.com` fail |

## Checklist

### 1. Find every caller

- Search your code for `commentanalyzer.googleapis.com`, `comments:analyze`, `perspective-api-client`, `peRspective`, `discourse-perspective-api` and `GOOGLE_API_DOMAIN`.
- Check plugins and bots you did not write: Discourse, Discord moderation bots, CMS comment plugins.
- Check offline uses: research scripts, dashboards and stored scores that assume Perspective's 0–1 TOXICITY scale.

### 2. Write down what each caller depends on

- Which attributes (TOXICITY, SEVERE_TOXICITY, INSULT, THREAT, IDENTITY_ATTACK, PROFANITY, SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT, or the experimental ones).
- Which languages.
- Which thresholds trigger an action (hide, queue for review, block).
- Whether anything parses `spanScores`, `languages` or `clientToken`.

### 3. Choose a replacement

| If you need… | Choose |
|---|---|
| No code changes; same request and JSON | A wire-compatible drop-in such as the [Perspective drop-in on Apify](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/perspective-api-alternative/) ($1 per 1,000 comments) |
| Free, and you can rewrite the call and re-tune | OpenAI's moderation endpoint (`omni-moderation-latest`, free) |
| You already run on Azure | Azure AI Content Safety (free tier 5,000 text records a month) |
| Full control, no third party | Self-host the open [Detoxify](https://github.com/unitaryai/detoxify) models |

Only the first option keeps the Perspective request and response. The others use different categories and score scales, so thresholds and stored data need re-mapping.

### 4. Re-tune on your own comments

- Export a sample of a few hundred real comments, including borderline ones.
- Score them with both Perspective, while it still works, and the replacement.
- Compare decisions at your current thresholds, not just raw scores. Adjust thresholds until the hide/review/allow decisions match what you want.

### 5. Cut over safely

- Put the endpoint and credentials in configuration, not code.
- Run both side by side (shadow mode) for a week if you can.
- Switch before mid-December, not on December 31: holiday change freezes and the final-day rush are real risks.
- Keep the old code path behind a flag until January, then delete it.

### 6. After January 1, 2027

- Confirm nothing still calls `commentanalyzer.googleapis.com`. Watch your logs for its errors.
- Update documentation and runbooks that mention Perspective.

## Minimal change with the drop-in

With the drop-in, step 5 is a two-line diff: the host and the credential.

```diff
- POST https://commentanalyzer.googleapis.com/v1alpha1/comments:analyze?key=$GOOGLE_API_KEY
+ POST https://dropin-apis--perspective-compat.apify.actor/v1alpha1/comments:analyze
+ Authorization: Bearer $APIFY_TOKEN
```

Full curl, Python and Node.js examples are on the [Perspective API replacement page](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/perspective-api-alternative/).

## FAQ

### When exactly does the Perspective API stop working?

Google says the API will no longer be in service after 2026, meaning after December 31, 2026. Plan for requests to fail from January 1, 2027.

### Can I still request a Perspective API key or more quota?

No. Google handled usage and quota requests only until February 2026.

### Do I have to change my code to replace Perspective?

Only if you switch to a different API, such as OpenAI moderation or Azure AI Content Safety. With a wire-compatible drop-in, you change the host and the credential, and the request and response stay the same.

### Will scores be identical after the migration?

No replacement reproduces Google's private models exactly. Open Detoxify models agree on clear cases but can differ on borderline comments. Re-tune your thresholds on a sample of real comments before you cut over.

### What happens if I do nothing?

From January 1, 2027, calls to the Perspective API fail. Depending on your error handling, comments may then be published without screening or not published at all.

# Transcribe Audio URL to SRT — Whisper Speech to Text

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/transcribe-audio-url-to-srt/


**Give this Actor a direct URL to an audio or video file and it returns the transcript, timed segments, and ready-to-save SRT and VTT subtitles.** It runs open-source Whisper (`faster-whisper`) in 99 languages with automatic language detection, and bills per started minute of audio — no subscription.

## What it accepts

mp3, mp4, m4a, wav, webm, ogg, flac, mkv and more — any direct link to a media file you're allowed to process (your own storage, S3, a CDN, a podcast enclosure URL). **It does not download from YouTube, TikTok, Instagram or other platform pages** — pass a direct file link.

## Example input

```json
{
  "urls": ["https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/dd/Armstrong_Small_Step.ogg"],
  "language": "",
  "model": "small",
  "outputFormats": ["text", "segments", "srt", "vtt"],
  "maxMinutesPerFile": 60
}
```

Two models: `small` (default, more accurate, $0.014/min) and `base` (2–3× faster, less accurate, $0.006/min). Up to 500 URLs and 1 GB per file; `maxMinutesPerFile` (1–180) caps cost by cutting long files at that point and billing only the transcribed minutes.

## Example output (real run on Apify)

```json
{
  "url": "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/dd/Armstrong_Small_Step.ogg",
  "language": "en",
  "durationSec": 24.11,
  "billedMinutes": 1,
  "text": "I'm going to step off the land now. That's one small step for man. One giant leap for mankind.",
  "segments": [
    { "start": 3.38, "end": 15.18, "text": "I'm going to step off the land now." },
    { "start": 15.18, "end": 20.81, "text": "That's one small step for man." }
  ],
  "srt": "1\n00:00:03,380 --> 00:00:15,180\nI'm going to step off the land now.\n\n...",
  "vtt": "WEBVTT\n\n00:00:03.380 --> 00:00:15.180\nI'm going to step off the land now.\n\n...",
  "error": null
}
```

A file that can't be processed (404, a web page instead of a media file, no audio track) returns a row with `error` set and `billedMinutes: 0` — the run continues with the next file.

## How it compares

| Audio | `small` model | `base` model |
|---|---|---|
| 30-second voice note | $0.014 | $0.006 |
| 10-minute speech | $0.14 | $0.06 |
| 1-hour podcast | $0.84 | $0.36 |

Measured on Apify's default 2 GB memory, a 10.3-minute speech took 7 minutes with `small`; at 4 GB it took under 4 minutes, and `base` took 1.5 minutes. Accuracy is that of the open Whisper **small** model: good on clear speech, weaker than large commercial models on noisy audio, heavy accents and rare languages.

## Run it from code

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient
client = ApifyClient(os.environ["APIFY_TOKEN"])
run = client.actor("dropin-apis/media-url-transcriber").call(run_input={
    "urls": ["https://example.com/podcast/episode-12.mp3"],
    "outputFormats": ["text", "srt"],
})
```

Agents connected to the [Apify MCP server](https://mcp.apify.com) can find it with `search-actors` ("transcribe audio") and run it with `call-actor`.

## Pricing

Pay per started minute of transcribed audio, plus Apify's standard run-start charge. **$0.014/minute** (`small`, default) or **$0.006/minute** (`base`). No subscription; failed files are not charged, and a maximum-charge budget on the run is checked before each file, stopping cleanly rather than over-billing.

**[Open the Whisper Audio & Video URL Transcriber on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/media-url-transcriber)**

## FAQ

### How do I transcribe an MP4 video to text?

Pass the direct URL of the .mp4 file in `urls`. The Actor extracts the audio track automatically and returns the transcript, segments, SRT and VTT.

### Can I make SRT or VTT subtitles from an audio file?

Yes — include `srt` and/or `vtt` in `outputFormats` (both are included by default), and each result row has ready-to-save subtitle text.

### Does it work with YouTube or TikTok links?

No. The Actor does not download from video or music platforms. Use a direct link to a media file you have the right to process.

### Which languages are supported?

All 99 Whisper languages, including English, Arabic, Spanish, French, German, Hindi, Chinese and Japanese, detected per file unless you set `language`.

### What does it cost?

$0.014 per started minute with the default `small` model ($0.84/hour), or $0.006/minute with `base` ($0.36/hour). Failed files are not charged.

### Is my audio stored anywhere?

No. Each file is downloaded to a temporary file inside the run, transcribed, and deleted. Only the transcript is saved to your dataset.

### I need an OpenAI whisper-1 compatible endpoint instead

Use the sister Actor, the [whisper-1 alternative](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/whisper-1-alternative/) — the same engine behind OpenAI's `/v1/audio/transcriptions` request and response format, for apps already built on the OpenAI SDK.

# tts-1 deprecated (Jan 6, 2027): a compatible /v1/audio/speech endpoint

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/tts-1-alternative/


**OpenAI is removing `tts-1`, `tts-1-hd` and both `gpt-4o-mini-tts` snapshots from the API on 6 January 2027.** This Actor accepts the same `POST /v1/audio/speech` request shape — you change the base URL and the API key, nothing else in your request body — and returns synthesized audio from independent local voices, from **$0.009 per 1,000 input characters**.

## What changes on 2027-01-06

OpenAI's own [deprecations page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations) states: *"The following text-to-speech models are deprecated and will be removed from the API on January 6, 2027, with at least three months' notice."* Announced 1 October 2026, the four models removed are `tts-1`, `tts-1-hd`, `gpt-4o-mini-tts-2025-03-20` and `gpt-4o-mini-tts-2025-12-15`. OpenAI's recommended replacement is `gpt-realtime-2.1-mini` — but that model prices audio by the **token** ($20 per 1M audio output tokens), not by the simple per-character rate `tts-1` had, so it is not a drop-in price comparison, only a drop-in *capability* successor aimed more at realtime voice agents than one-shot text-to-speech calls. After 6 January 2027, any code still calling `tts-1`/`tts-1-hd`/`gpt-4o-mini-tts` will fail outright, not degrade gracefully.

## Minimal migration diff

Only the base URL and the auth header change — model, voice, format and other parameters stay in the same place in the request body:

```diff
  client = OpenAI(
-     api_key=os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"],
+     api_key=os.environ["APIFY_TOKEN"],
+     base_url="https://dropin-apis--tts-compat.apify.actor/v1",
  )
  with client.audio.speech.with_streaming_response.create(
      model="tts-1", input="Hello, world.", voice="amber", response_format="wav"
  ) as response:
      response.stream_to_file("speech.wav")
```

Or plain HTTP:

```bash
curl --fail-with-body \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"model":"tts-1","input":"Hello, world.","voice":"amber","response_format":"mp3"}' \
  'https://dropin-apis--tts-compat.apify.actor/v1/audio/speech' \
  --output speech.mp3
```

Confirm the real deployed hostname on the Actor's **Endpoints** tab before going live. `model` is accepted as a compatibility identifier only — `tts-1`, `tts-1-hd` and `gpt-4o-mini-tts` all select the **same** local model underneath, with no HD/quality tier. `voice` accepts the same parameter *values* (`alloy`, `echo`, `nova`, and so on) mapped to distinct independent local voices — re-test pronunciation and voice choice, since the acoustic output is different. Remove any nonempty `instructions` or SSE `stream_format` options: both return HTTP 400 here.

## How it compares

| Option | Price | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **This Actor (Standby)** | $0.009 per 1,000 characters | Independent local Kokoro voices, English only, compatible request/response shape, no voice cloning |
| **This Actor (Store/MCP batch run)** | $0.12 per 1,000 characters | Same voices; use for longer inputs — see the latency note below |
| OpenAI's recommended replacement (`gpt-realtime-2.1-mini`) | $20 per 1M audio output tokens | Token-priced realtime-voice-agent model, not a simple per-character TTS rate — needs its own cost modeling, not a straight swap |
| [Kokoro Text to Speech on Apify](https://apify.com/conserving_celerytop/kokoro-text-to-speech) | $0.08 per 1,000 characters (per its own Store listing) | Also Kokoro-based; 54 voices across 9 languages advertised, vs. this Actor's 13 English-only voices |
| Self-hosting Kokoro or Piper yourself | Your compute, no per-call fee | No managed endpoint, no OpenAI-compatible request shape out of the box, you run and scale it |

**This is an independent speech service, not an OpenAI product.** Compatibility covers the request shape and the audio response format — not identical voices, pronunciation, prosody or model quality, and there is no affiliation with OpenAI or any other provider. Every successful response carries `X-Voice-Provider` and `X-Local-Voice` disclosure headers naming the actual local voice used. The `voice` parameter values above (`alloy`, `echo`, etc.) are accepted **only as compatibility identifiers** so existing request bodies keep working — they are not a claim that you get OpenAI's own voices.

## Honest latency note

Real measured runs, not estimates: a live 1,000-character normal (batch) run on Apify took **151.192 seconds** total; a 4,096-character run took **760.015 seconds**, both at the default 4 GB. Locally (excluding cloud platform/container startup), cold synthesis at 4 GB measured 49.893s for 1,000 characters and 199.511s for 4,096. **Use the Standby endpoint only for short inputs** — a long buffered HTTP call can exceed its ~270-second synthesis deadline and the platform's five-minute first-response budget, returning HTTP 503 with no audio and no character charge. For longer text, use a normal Store or MCP run instead (up to 4,096 characters, 1,200-second timeout) — it costs more per character ($0.12 vs $0.009) specifically because it's built for exactly this case. There is no real-time guarantee either way; full measurements are in the Actor's own `VERIFY.md`.

## Pricing

Pay per event, no subscription. Standby `characters-1k`: **$0.009** per started 1,000 Unicode characters (spaces count), e.g. 250 or 1,000 characters cost $0.009, 1,001 cost $0.018, 4,096 cost $0.045. Normal Store/MCP `batch-characters-1k`: **$0.12** per started 1,000 characters — 4,096 characters cost $0.60. Validation and synthesis errors are never charged; a billing failure returns HTTP 503 with no audio delivered, and an exhausted spending cap returns HTTP 402.

**[Open Text-to-Speech API on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/tts-compat)**

## FAQ

### Is this the same model as OpenAI's tts-1?

No. It runs Kokoro-82M, an independent open local model, through quantized ONNX on CPU. The request and response shape are compatible so your existing client code keeps working; the voices, pronunciation and audio quality are not identical to OpenAI's.

### What happens to my code after January 6, 2027?

Any request to OpenAI's API naming `tts-1`, `tts-1-hd`, `gpt-4o-mini-tts-2025-03-20` or `gpt-4o-mini-tts-2025-12-15` will fail outright once OpenAI removes them — there is no quiet fallback. Point `base_url` at this Actor's endpoint and keep the rest of your request body unchanged to keep the same code path working.

### Does this support Arabic or other languages?

No — English only in this version. An unsupported script returns HTTP 400 rather than silently mangled audio.

### Why would a short, ordinary piece of text return an error?

The no-espeak English pronunciation lexicon doesn't cover every spelling, so an unrecognized name or acronym is rejected (HTTP 400) rather than silently mispronounced or dropped. Rephrase or spell it out.

### Can an AI agent call this through Apify MCP?

Yes — a normal `call-actor` run synthesizes the text and returns one dataset row with a downloadable audio URL, billed at the batch rate ($0.12 per 1,000 characters). An HTTP-capable agent can call the cheaper Standby endpoint ($0.009) directly instead.

### What audio formats are supported?

MP3 (default), Opus, AAC, FLAC, WAV and headerless PCM (signed 16-bit little-endian, mono, 24 kHz) — decode PCM with explicit parameters; it is not a WAV file.
